statement: In the Turin economy (seed 7), the family that ends up owning the city is decided within its first day, before its share of the cars says so: replays rewound to later hours of day 0 return the same winner far more often than replays from hour 0.
cmd: REPS=32 DAYS=4 EVERY=3 SPAN=24 node tools/replay.mjs turin 7 (then FREEZE=1)
predicted: hour 0: under 20% of replays; above 75% by hour 18; the rise comes before the family holds half the cars; frozen null similar to evolving
note: redesigned 2026-10-30 before any replay finished: the base run showed the winner already held 54% of the cars by the end of day 0, so days 1 and 5 were too late to rewind to
result: Turin s7, 32 replays per hour: evolving 0/32, 1/32, 15/32, 22/32 at hours 0, 3, 6, 9, then 32/32 from hour 12; frozen 0/32, 1/32, 21/32, 27/32, then 31-32/32. Decided between hours 3 and 12 of day 0, before the family holds half the cars (37-40% at hours 6-9). Not driven by evolution: with mutation frozen the winner is if anything surer (hours 6+9: 48/64 frozen vs 37/64 evolving, Fisher p=0.06). One seed; a second is next.

statement: An all-day congestion charge (0.1) cuts crashes per car and trip time and costs fares, in Turin.
cmd: SEEDS=20 node tools/trial.mjs turin congestion=0.1
predicted: fares -10 to -25%, crashes per car -15 to -25%, trip time -20 to -30%, all intervals excluding zero
result: 20 seeds (101-120), days 2-6: fares -17.8% [-20.5, -15.1], crashes per car -24.0% [-27.0, -21.0], trip time -29.0% [-30.6, -27.4], cars -44.8% [-47.1, -42.5], Gini +0.005 [+0.004, +0.006]; every seed the same direction. Within the predicted ranges.

statement: The decision window found for Turin seed 7 (the winner's replay win rate rising from near 0 at hour 3 to every replay by hour 12 of day 0) is not a quirk of that seed: on Turin seed 11 the winning family is also decided within day 0, before it holds half the cars.
cmd: REPS=32 DAYS=4 EVERY=3 SPAN=24 node tools/replay.mjs turin 11 (then FREEZE=1)
predicted: hour 0: under 20% of replays; above 75% by hour 12; the winner's share under 50% at the hour the rate passes 75%; frozen similar to evolving. If the curve is flat or only rises after day 0, the C1 result is seed-specific.
note: statement corrected 2026-10-30 before any seed 11 result: it first said 'decided by hour six', from a table that counted survival as winning; predictions unchanged
result: Killed. Correct counts (win = over half the cars), hours 0-21: evolving 3,7,12,11,19,9,16,15 of 32; frozen 6,3,8,9,8,3,26,27 of 32. Not decided on day 0 while evolving; frozen decides it from hour 18. An earlier version of this result counted survival as winning (corrected 2026-10-30).

statement: Insurance (crash costs pooled into a flat premium) roughly doubles crashes per car and raises fares, in Turin.
cmd: SEEDS=20 node tools/trial.mjs turin insurance=1
predicted: crashes per car +60 to +120%, fares up 10 to 40%, intervals excluding zero
source: README, Rules and prices: 'Insure drivers and they crash twice as often, and move a third more people'
result: 20 seeds, days 2-6: fares +34.3% [+31.5, +37.2], crashes per car +86.5% [+82.1, +91.1], trip time -35.8% [-37.4, -34.2], cars +65.4% [+59.5, +71.1], Gini +0.051 [+0.046, +0.055]; every seed the same direction. Within the predicted ranges; 'twice' is really +87%.

statement: Credit (a car may run 30 units into debt before it counts as broke) raises fares by a fifth to a quarter and crashes per car by about as much, in Turin.
cmd: SEEDS=20 node tools/trial.mjs turin credit=30
predicted: fares +15 to +30%, crashes per car +15 to +30%, intervals excluding zero
source: README, Rules and prices: 'An overdraft raises fares by a fifth to a quarter and crashes as much' (the 30 is my guess at the original setting, from tools/policies.mjs)
result: fares +28.0% [+26.0,+29.7], crashes per car +25.2% [+22.4,+28.1], trip time +21.0% [+18.0,+24.0], cars +60.2%, Gini +0.291; all 20 seeds up. Predictions held; README 'a fifth to a quarter' was slightly low for fares.

statement: The Turin finding (a monopoly winner is mostly decided during day 0, replay win rate rising steeply over the first hours) also holds on another city: Barcelona, seed 7.
cmd: REPS=32 DAYS=4 EVERY=3 SPAN=24 node tools/replay.mjs barcelona 7 (then FREEZE=1)
predicted: hour 0: under 50% of replays; 75% or more by hour 12; frozen similar to evolving. If the curve is flat from hour 0 or only rises after day 0, the Turin result is a Turin quirk.
result: Barcelona s7, 32 replays per hour, evolving, same winner (family 59, 60% of the cars at the end): h0 1/32, h3 2/32, h6 13/32, h9 8/32, h12 13/32, h15 10/32, h18 14/32, h21 17/32 (h12: 26-58%, h21: 36-69%, Wilson 95%). Hour 0 under 50% as predicted, but 75% or more by hour 12 failed: the rate rises from near zero to about 40% by hour 6 and then stays at 25-53% through hour 21, with the winner holding 24-38% of the cars. On Barcelona the winner is only partly decided by day 0. Frozen run on hours 0, 6, 12, 21 launched, not part of this verdict.

statement: Mutation keeps the contest for the city open: replayed from the same moment, an economy with mutation frozen returns the original winner more often than one still evolving.
cmd: for s in 21 22 23 24 25 26: REPS=16 DAYS=4 EVERY=12 SPAN=24 node tools/replay.mjs turin $s 12 (and FREEZE=1)
predicted: pooled over six fresh Turin seeds, rewound to hour 12: frozen wins at least 10 percentage points more often than evolving, in at least 4 of 6 seeds; Fisher exact on the pooled counts p < 0.05
source: hint from C1 (seed 7, hours 6+9: 48/64 frozen vs 37/64) and C3 (seed 11, hours 18-21: 53/64 vs 31/64), both picked after the fact, hence fresh seeds
result: Turin hour 12, 16 replays per cell, winner replays (evolving vs frozen): s21 1 vs 1, s22 6 vs 2, s23 4 vs 1, s24 16 vs 16, s25 9 vs 7, s26 16 vs 16. Pooled 52/96 evolving, 43/96 frozen. Frozen never beat evolving, so 0 of 6 seeds met the +10 points bar; pooled Fisher exact two-sided p = 0.248. Direction is opposite to the prediction. C1 and C3 hints (seeds 7, 11) do not generalise to hour 12 on fresh seeds.

statement: A third city, Venice seed 7, behaves like Barcelona and Turin seed 11 rather than Turin seed 7: the original winner is not yet decided by hour 12 of day 0.
cmd: REPS=32 DAYS=4 EVERY=6 SPAN=24 node tools/replay.mjs venice 7
predicted: hour 0 under 25% of replays won by the original winner; hour 12 under 75%
source: Study 1 item 4; C6 killed the Turin-s7 curve on Barcelona
result: Venice s7, 32 replays per hour, winner (family 85, ends 97% of cars) replays: hour 0 0/32 (0-11%), hour 6 8/32 (13-42%), hour 12 14/32 (28-61%), hour 18 26/32 (65-91%). Hour 0 under 25% and hour 12 under 75% both held; decided only by hour 18, at 22% share.

statement: The biggest family stays biggest is beaten: on fresh runs, a family holding under half the cars wins replays more often than its share says.
cmd: REPS=32 DAYS=4 EVERY=3 SPAN=18 node tools/replay.mjs venice 8 (and barcelona 8)
predicted: pooled over both runs, at snapshots from hour 3 on where the winner holds under 50% of the cars: the 95% Wilson interval of the replay win rate lies above the share in at least 60% of them and below it in at most 1. If not, the share explains the curve.
source: Study 1 step 3 exploratory table (11 of 20 above, 8 contain, 1 below), written before the fresh run
result: Fresh Venice s8 and Barcelona s8, 32 replays per hour. Snapshots from hour 3 on with the winner under 50% of the cars: 9 pooled. The win-rate interval lies above the share in 5 (Venice hours 3, 6, 12, 15; Barcelona hour 15), contains it in 4, below in 0. 5 of 9 is under the 60% bar, so the share explains the curve.

statement: Barcelona's real one-way arrows cost fares: the same streets two-way carry more, and are no more dangerous.
cmd: SEEDS=20 ALT=tmp/barcelona-twoway.json node tools/trial.mjs barcelona
predicted: two-way vs one-way: fares +10 to +35% with an interval excluding zero; crashes per car within +-15% (no safety benefit to the arrows)
source: README, Rules and prices: 'One-way streets do not pay here... a sixth to a fifth fewer fares... and are no safer'
result: Barcelona, 20 seeds, days 2-6, two-way vs one-way (tmp/trial-oneway.log): fares a day +18.2% [+15.7%, +20.6%], 20 up / 0 down; crashes per car a day -0.9% [-3.6%, +1.7%], not distinguishable from zero; trip time -17.5% [-20.2%, -14.8%]; cars -2.9% [-6.7%, +0.7%]. Both parts of the prediction hold.

statement: The safety-for-fares trade of the all-day congestion charge is about the economy, not about evolution: with mutation frozen after day 2 in both arms, the charge still lowers crashes per car and still costs fares.
cmd: SEEDS=20 FREEZE=1 node tools/trial.mjs turin congestion=0.1
predicted: frozen, Turin, twenty seeds: crashes per car down with a 95% interval entirely below zero, fares down with an interval entirely below zero. If either interval spans zero, the trade needs evolving drivers.
source: Study 2; README, Rules and prices: the charge at twenty seeds (evolving arm). Queued after C10 (tmp/c11.sh)
result: Turin, congestion=0.1 vs no rule, mutation frozen after day 2 in both arms, 20 seeds, days 2-6 (tmp/trial-frozen-charge.log): crashes per car a day -31.4% [-35.0%, -27.7%], 0 up / 20 down; fares a day -15.0% [-18.5%, -11.6%], 0 up / 20 down; trip time -28.8% [-31.9%, -25.4%]; cars -43.3% [-46.4%, -40.4%]. Both intervals entirely below zero, as predicted: the trade is about the economy, not evolution.

statement: The safety-for-fares trade of the all-day congestion charge needs no evolution at all: with a hand-written driver that cannot evolve, the charge still lowers crashes per car and still costs fares.
cmd: FOUNDERS=hand SEEDS=20 node tools/trial.mjs turin congestion=0.1
predicted: hand-written drivers, Turin, twenty seeds: crashes per car down with a 95% interval entirely below zero, fares down with an interval entirely below zero. If either interval spans zero or fares rise, the trade needs learned drivers.
source: Study 2, third arm (src/hand.js); C11 (frozen evolved drivers) confirmed; written before the run
result: Turin, congestion=0.1 vs no rule, hand-written drivers (src/hand.js) in both arms, 20 seeds, days 2-6 (tmp/trial-hand-charge.log): crashes per car a day -40.3% [-48.6%, -33.0%], 0 up / 20 down; fares a day -57.0% [-68.8%, -45.8%], 0 up / 20 down; trip time -25.2% [-33.6%, -16.5%]; cars -44.6% [-55.1%, -33.5%]. Both intervals entirely below zero, as predicted: the trade needs no evolution at all.

statement: Barcelona's one-way arrows cost fares without evolution too: with hand-written drivers that cannot evolve, the same streets two-way still carry more, and are no more dangerous.
cmd: FOUNDERS=hand SEEDS=20 ALT=tmp/barcelona-twoway.json node tools/trial.mjs barcelona
predicted: two-way vs one-way, hand-written drivers, twenty seeds: fares up with a 95% interval entirely above zero; crashes per car within +-15% (interval inside it). If fares do not rise, the one-way cost needed learned drivers.
source: Study 2; C10 (evolving drivers) confirmed; written before the run
result: Barcelona, 20 seeds, days 2-6, two-way vs one-way, hand-written drivers (tmp/trial-hand-oneway.log): fares a day +3767.1% [+913.7%, +7311.0%], 16 up / 4 down; crashes per car a day +276.1% [+85.4%, +498.8%], 17 up / 3 down; cars +234.9% [+69.9%, +428.2%]; trip time +25.8% [-9.3%, +67.0%]. Fares rise with an interval above zero, but crashes per car are far outside +-15%, so the prediction fails. Mean fares a day over the seeds 1258.6 one-way against 2030.7 two-way, cars 133.0 against 203.1 (from the run telemetry); the huge percentages come from seeds where the one-way baseline had almost no fares, so the per-seed ratio is unstable. The no-safety-benefit half of C10 does not carry over to drivers that cannot evolve.

statement: Letting a broke taxi finish its ride and pooling crash costs raises fares a day well above no rule, at twenty seeds.
cmd: SEEDS=20 node tools/trial.mjs turin finishFare=1,insurance=1
predicted: fares a day up by +40% to +150% with a 95% interval entirely above zero (the README's 4768 against 2476 is one seed, +93%).
source: README, What it has found, via tools/reap.mjs; written before the run
result: Turin, finishFare=1,insurance=1 vs no rule, 20 seeds, days 2-6 (tmp/trial-failure-rules.log): fares a day +86.8% [+81.9%, +91.1%], 20 up / 0 down; crashes per car a day +91.4% [+87.0%, +95.9%], 20 up / 0 down; trip time -22.7% [-24.5%, -20.7%]; cars +101.5% [+95.3%, +107.8%]; Gini +0.132 [+0.126, +0.138]. Fares up within +40% to +150% with the interval above zero, as predicted. The README also says "more than any change to the drivers"; that comparison was not run here.

statement: In fog the drivers speed up: with every car's sight halved, distance covered per tick rises, at twenty seeds.
cmd: SEEDS=20 FOG=0.5 node tools/drunk.mjs
predicted: distance per tick up with a 95% interval entirely above zero. Crashes per 1000 units are reported, not predicted.
source: README, What it has found: 'In fog they speed up'. A two-seed smoke run of the new SEEDS= mode (+20.4% distance per tick) was seen before this was written; the twenty seeds are 101-120
result: 20 seeds (101-120), every car's sight halved against none, shipped drivers in a traffic city (tmp/drunk-fog.log): distance per tick +20.7% [+20.0%, +21.5%], 20 up / 0 down; crashes per 1000 units -5.5% [-6.8%, -4.2%], 0 up / 20 down. Distance per tick up with the interval above zero, as predicted. Crashes fall a little in fog (not predicted).

statement: A fifth of a second of reaction delay, on every car, quadruples crashes, at twenty seeds.
cmd: SEEDS=20 DELAY=12 SHARE=1 node tools/drunk.mjs
predicted: crashes per 1000 units up with a 95% interval entirely above +150% (a quadrupling is +300%). If the interval includes +150% or lies below it, 'quadruples' is overstated.
source: README, What it has found: 'They are reflex machines'; the original was three seeds (NOTEBOOK, slow reactions). Written before the run
result: 20 seeds (101-120), every car acting on what it saw 12 ticks (0.2 s) ago against none (tmp/drunk-delay.log): crashes per 1000 units +291.6% [+285.0%, +298.4%], 20 up / 0 down; distance per tick -63.7% [-64.2%, -63.2%]. The interval lies entirely above +150% (a quadrupling is +300%, just above its top), as predicted.

statement: One family takes the city without any evolution: with hand-written drivers that cannot evolve, one founder's family still owns over half the cars at day 6, in most runs.
cmd: FOUNDERS=hand SEEDS=20 node tools/families.mjs turin
predicted: hand-written drivers, Turin, twenty seeds, six days: a family owns over half the cars in at least 15 of 20 runs (the Wilson 95% interval then lies above 50%). If fewer, the takeover needed evolving drivers. The same twenty seeds with evolved drivers are reported, not predicted.
source: Study 2, dynasty takeover three ways; README 'One family takes the city' (three of four runs, evolved); written before the run
result: Turin, six days, 20 seeds (101-120), hand-written drivers (tmp/families-hand.log): a family owns over half the cars in 12 of 20 runs (Wilson 95% [39%, 78%]); in none of the 20 does a single family own every car (0 of 20); mean share of the biggest family 46.75%. The prediction needed at least 15 of 20: 12 is short, so the takeover was not shown to need no evolution. Context, the same seeds with evolved drivers (tmp/families-evolved.log): over half in 19 of 20 (Wilson [76%, 99%]), a single family owning every car in 8 of 20 (Wilson [22%, 61%]), mean share 79.1%.

statement: NEAT's species threshold moving 0.02 a generation, not 0.3, does better from scratch: at twenty seeds, the generation-based city's mean fitness is higher with the small step.
cmd: SEEDS=20 GENS=100 TAIL=20 node tools/stepcmp.mjs
predicted: mean fitness over generations 81-100, step 0.02 minus step 0.3, paired over twenty seeds: a positive mean with a 95% interval entirely above zero. If the interval includes zero, 'evolution does better from scratch' (README: three seeds of three) was luck.
source: README, About the method itself: 'A flaw in NEAT's species control'; reaper plan. A two-seed 60-generation smoke run (-33.5, interval spanning zero) was seen first, so GENS=100 and TAIL=20 were chosen before the real run, not tuned on it
result: Generation-based city from scratch, twenty seeds (101-120), 100 generations, mean fitness over generations 81-100 (tmp/stepcmp.log): step 0.3 gives 135.6, step 0.02 gives 112.1; difference (0.02 minus 0.3) -23.4 [-55.0, +6.0], 9 up / 11 down. The interval includes zero and the point estimate is negative, so the prediction (interval entirely above zero) fails: the README's "evolution does better from scratch" with the small step, seen on three seeds, is not borne out at twenty.

statement: Real one-way cities are fragile: with 5% of the road segments closed at random, only about half of Turin, Barcelona and Manhattan still all reach each other, and a grid keeps nearly all, on closure orders not used before.
cmd: for m in turin barcelona manhattan grid; do ORDER0=1000 node tools/percolation.mjs $m | tail -1; done
predicted: twenty fresh closure orders per city (seeds 1000-1019): the 95% interval of the share still all connected at 5% closed lies within 35% to 70% for Turin, Barcelona and Manhattan, and its lower bound is at least 97% for the grid.
source: README, The street network: 'Close 5% of road segments at random and half of Turin, Barcelona or Manhattan can no longer reach the rest; a grid loses 1%'; the table of means over orders 100-119 (53%, 56%, 59%, grid 99%) was seen before; the orders here are new
result: Twenty fresh closure orders per city (ORDER0=1000, tmp/percolation-c19.log), 5% of roads closed: Turin 46.1% still all connected, 95% interval 38.5%-53.5%; Barcelona 60.8%, 54.2%-67.0%; Manhattan 55.6%, 48.8%-61.6%; grid 99.4%, 99.1%-99.8%. The three real cities lie within 35% to 70% and the grid lower bound is above 97%, as predicted.

statement: A side of the road, by chance: with Turin's cars on twenty fresh seeds, most runs keep to one side by day 4, and which side is a coin flip.
cmd: node tools/sides.mjs "runs/trial-turin-base-d6-s{s}"
predicted: day 4, twenty seeds (101-120, the no-rule arm of the Turin trials): at least 15 of 20 runs have 75% or more of the cars on their majority side (Wilson lower bound then above 50%), and the number of runs whose majority side is the right is between 6 and 14 (exact binomial p above 0.05). Outside that, the README's 'three in four to nine in ten' or 'by chance' fails.
source: README, What evolves with no fitness function: 'A side of the road, by chance'; reaper plan. The telemetry of these runs was not looked at for this before the prediction
result: Turin, day 4, twenty seeds (101-120, the no-rule arm of the Turin trials, tmp/sides-c20.log): the share of cars on the run's majority side runs from 0.51 to 0.83 (median 0.67 of the rounded values); 7 of 20 runs keep one side at 0.75 or more (Wilson 95% [18%, 57%]); 8 of 20 keep the right (exact binomial p 0.503). The prediction needed at least 15 of 20 at 0.75 or more: 7 is far short, so killed. The coin-flip half held: 8 of 20 keep the right, inside the predicted 6 to 14.

statement: Drivers spread across two competing platforms as the ideal free distribution predicts, at twenty seeds: in proportion to what each pays out, without any driver choosing.
cmd: SEEDS=20 B=0.7 CA=0.1 CB=0.4 node tools/platforms.mjs turin
predicted: Turin, six days, twenty seeds (101-120), B books 70% of passengers, commissions 10% and 40%, one child in twenty switches: the share of drivers on B at the end (mean of the last day's two samples) less the ideal free distribution (60.9%) has a 95% interval lying inside -10 to +10 points.
source: README, What evolves with no fitness function: 'Drivers spread across competing platforms as ecology predicts'; the original was one run (NOTEBOOK, two platforms); written before the twenty seeds
result: Turin, six days, twenty seeds (101-120), B books 0.7, commissions 0.1 and 0.4, switch 0.05 (tmp/platforms-c21.log): drivers on B at the end 59.5% against the ideal free distribution 60.9%; difference -1.3 points [-2.5, -0.0], 4 above / 16 below. The interval lies inside -10 to +10 points, as predicted; it sits just below zero, so the drivers are slightly under-represented on B.

statement: A hand-driver Turin city starts more reliably from 100 starting cars than from 50: whether it leaves its floor is luck, and a bigger start improves the odds.
cmd: SEEDS=20 START=50,100,150 node tools/starts.mjs turin
predicted: Turin, hand-written drivers, two days, twenty seeds (101-120): at startCars 100, at least 18 of 20 runs end with more than 30 cars (the Wilson lower bound is then above 70%). At 50 and 150 the counts are reported, not predicted. For orientation, the six-day C12 hand runs at the default 50 had 16 of 20 above 30.
source: Backlog, what decides the start; the one-seed start-cars experiment (seed 104: 100 thrives, 50 and 200 collapse) was seen before this was written
result: Turin, hand-written drivers, two days, twenty seeds (101-120), runs ending with more than 30 cars (tmp/starts-c22.log): startCars 50: 16 of 20 (Wilson 95% [58%, 92%]); 100: 16 of 20 ([58%, 92%]); 150: 17 of 20 ([64%, 95%]). The prediction needed at least 18 of 20 at 100: 16 is short, so killed. The start rate is about four in five at every setting tried; a bigger start does not help.

statement: Yielding does not pay: a coded rule that brakes hard near a junction when a side ray sees a car closing in lowers the drivers' fitness and does not lower their crashes per car, at twenty seeds.
cmd: SEEDS=20 node tools/yieldrule.mjs
predicted: traffic cities, twenty seeds (101-120), the 'rule' arm against none, paired: fitness down with a 95% interval entirely below zero, and crashes per car not down (the interval does not lie entirely below zero). The 'wide' arm is reported, not predicted. If crashes per car fall with the interval below zero, yielding does pay in safety.
source: README, What it has found: 'They queue but do not yield'; reaper plan. A two-seed smoke run of the new mode (rule fitness -5.4% [-6.4%, -4.4%], crashes per car +0.1%) was seen before this was written
result: Traffic cities, twenty seeds (101-120), the coded rule (brake hard near a junction when a side ray sees a car closing in) against none, paired (tmp/yieldrule-c23.log): fitness -4.1% [-5.0%, -3.2%], 0 up / 20 down; trips per car -6.6% [-7.2%, -6.1%]; crashes per car +0.6% [-0.1%, +1.3%], 12 up / 8 down, not distinguishable from zero. The wide arm: fitness -4.8% [-5.6%, -4.0%], trips per car -9.4% [-10.0%, -8.7%], crashes per car +0.8% [-0.1%, +1.7%]. Fitness down with the interval below zero and crashes not down, as predicted.

statement: The cold-start trap belongs to the hand driver, not to the economy: with the evolved founders, a Turin city starts even from very few cars.
cmd: FOUNDERS=docs/trained.json SEEDS=20 START=10,20 node tools/starts.mjs turin
predicted: evolved founders (free to evolve), Turin, two days, twenty seeds (101-120): at startCars 10 and at 20, at least 18 of 20 runs end with more than 30 cars each. If fewer, the trap is in the economy's cold start, not the hand driver.
source: Backlog, the cold-start trap; C22 (hand drivers start in about four of five whatever the start); the evolved Turin trials at the default 50 had 0 of 20 collapsed (tools/collapse.mjs). Written before the run
result: Turin, evolved founders free to evolve, two days, twenty seeds (101-120), runs ending with more than 30 cars (tmp/starts-c24.log): startCars 10: 20 of 20 (Wilson 95% [84%, 100%]); startCars 20: 20 of 20 ([84%, 100%]). At least 18 of 20 at each was predicted: holds. The cold-start trap is the hand driver's (16 of 20 at 50, 16 at 100, 17 at 150, C22), not the economy's.

statement: The cheapest car wins: with no freight pay in the default Turin economy, the cars evolve smaller and shorter-sighted, in nearly every run, on seeds not looked at before.
cmd: seeds 121-140: node headless.mjs --eco --run runs/traits-turin-s{seed} --days 6 --founders docs/trained.json --seed {seed} --map turin; node tools/traits.mjs "runs/traits-turin-s{s}" (with seeds from 121)
predicted: Turin, six days, twenty new seeds (121-140), no rule: the population's mean body length, mean sight range gene and mean cargo gene are lower at the end than at the start in at least 18 of 20 runs each (sign test p below 0.001), and the mean rays gene is higher in at least 18 of 20.
source: README, What evolves with no fitness function: 'The cheapest car wins, small and short-sighted'; reaper plan. The same measure on seeds 101-120 (length, range, cargo fell in 20 of 20, rays rose in 20 of 20) was seen before this was written, so the claim is for seeds 121-140, which were not looked at
result: Turin, six days, twenty new seeds (121-140), no rule, evolved founders (tmp/traits-c25.log): mean body trait at the end less at the start, 95% interval, runs where it fell: length -0.277 [-0.290, -0.265] fell in 20 of 20; range -0.136 [-0.170, -0.101] fell in 20 of 20; cargo -0.245 [-0.267, -0.226] fell in 20 of 20; rays +0.113 [+0.082, +0.146] rose in 19 of 20 (fell in 1). Also width -0.257 (20 of 20 fell), engine -0.103 (17 of 20), jam -0.126 (19 of 20), brakes +0.005 (10 of 20, no drift). All four predicted counts are at least 18 of 20: confirmed.

statement: The drivers generalise to cities they never saw, and do better on real streets: at twenty seeds they crash less per 1000 units driven in Turin, Barcelona and Manhattan than in the generated cities they were raised in.
cmd: for m in "" turin barcelona manhattan; do MAP=$m ARMS=none SEEDS=20 node tools/yieldrule.mjs; done
predicted: traffic cities, no rule, twenty seeds (101-120): the 95% interval of crashes per 1000 units driven in each of Turin, Barcelona and Manhattan lies entirely below the interval for the generated cities (the intervals do not overlap).
source: README, What it has found: 'Drivers generalise to cities they never saw' (2.8, 1.4 and 1.3 against 3.5, from three-seed runs of this same tool, seen before: 2.79 Turin, 1.35 Barcelona, 1.27 Manhattan, 3.52 generated); the seeds here are 101-120; written before the twenty-seed run
result: Traffic cities, no rule, twenty seeds (101-120), crashes per 1000 units driven with a 95% interval (tmp/yr-c26-*.log): generated cities 3.58 [3.53, 3.63]; Turin 2.81 [2.78, 2.83]; Barcelona 1.39 [1.36, 1.41]; Manhattan 1.27 [1.25, 1.28]. Each real city lies entirely below the generated cities, as predicted. The intervals are narrow because a seed here is one traffic city of 120 cars over six generations and the seeds differ only in the traffic.

statement: The cheapest car wins unless freight pays: with freight pay and demand tripled, the cargo gene rises instead of falling, on fresh seeds.

correction: 2026-10-31: the hand drivers do not lean left. 6-8% of their samples are exactly on the centreline and the side metric counts lateral > 0 only as right, so ties read as left (seed 221: above zero 0.457, below zero 0.459).
